title: Integral saturated stalks and section monoids of fs log structures on arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme, with no Noetherian hypothesis. A log structure on $X$ means a sheaf of commutative monoids $M$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with $\alpha:M\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ inducing an isomorphism on units, as in the arbitrary-scheme convention of [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation]. For an etale $U\to X$, a finitely generated integral commutative monoid $P$ and a homomorphism $c:P\to\Gamma(U,M)$, put $\beta=\alpha c:P\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and let $L_U(P,\beta)$ be the associated log structure of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening]. Then $c$ is a chart when the homomorphism $L_U(P,\beta)\to M|_U$ corresponding to $c$ under the universal property of [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening] (for the identity of $U$) is an isomorphism. The log structure $M$ is fs when it admits etale-local charts by fine saturated monoids (finitely generated monoids embedding in their group completions and closed under positive roots there) [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. If $M$ is fs, then for every geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk $M_{\bar x}$, and for every etale $U\to X$ the section monoid $\Gamma(U,M)$, are integral and saturated: each embeds in its group completion, and an element $g$ of that group completion with $mg$ in the monoid for some integer $m>0$ lies in the monoid. No finite generation of these section monoids is asserted.

source.place: ILO VI 1.1, printed p.69, and VIII 3.3.3--3.3.6, printed pp.106--107; arbitrary-scheme associated-log conventions, referring to Kato (1988), section 1. The general stalk and section formulation is an agent refinement.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and an fs chart on a pointed etale neighbourhood, using the definition of fs in the statement. By [lem-per-integral-chart-logification-thickening], the chart identifies $M_{\bar x}$ with $C=P\oplus_E G$, where $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $G=A^\times$, $E=\beta^{-1}(A^\times)$ and $f:E\to G$ is induced by $\beta$. Here $P$ is finitely generated, integral and saturated. The stalk formula has no Noetherian hypothesis. Apply [lem-per-integral-monoid-unit-pushout] to embed $C$ in $H=(P^{\rm gp}\times G)/\{(e,-f^{\rm gp}(e)):e\in E^{\rm gp}\}$, now writing all monoids additively. This group is $C^{\rm gp}$: a homomorphism from $C$ to an abelian group is exactly a pair of homomorphisms from $P$ and $G$ agreeing on $E$, and extending the first to $P^{\rm gp}$ gives precisely the displayed quotient universal property. In particular the stalk is integral.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69; VIII 3.3.2--3.3.4, pp.106--107; agent calculation from the associated-log stalk formula

proof.text: For saturation of that stalk, take $h=[(z,g)]\in H$, $z\in P^{\rm gp}$, with $nh=[(p,v)]\in C$, $p\in P$, $n>0$. The quotient relation in $H$ implies $nz-p=e_1-e_2$ for some $e_1,e_2\in E$: every element of $E^{\rm gp}$ is such a difference. Hence $n(z+e_2)=p+e_1+(n-1)e_2\in P$. Saturation of $P$ gives $z+e_2\in P$. But $h=[(z+e_2,g-f(e_2))]$, which belongs to $C$. This proves saturation of every geometric stalk. No divisibility or torsion-freeness of $G$ is used.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101, saturation convention; agent three-line quotient calculation

proof.text: Let $U\to X$ be any etale object and put $B=M(U)$, additively. If $a+c=b+c$ in $B$, every geometric germ satisfies this equality in an integral stalk, so cancellation there gives $a_{\bar x}=b_{\bar x}$ for every geometric point and every lift to $U$. The exact section-equality statement of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sections-geometric-germ-ext], applied to the underlying set sheaf of $M$, gives $a=b$. Thus $B$ is cancellative. In the explicit group completion by differences, equality of the images of $a,b\in B$ means $a+c=b+c$ for some $c\in B$; cancellation proves that $B\to B^{\rm gp}$ is injective. This applies to every etale object, hence also to all overlaps used below.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks), injectivity; explicit cancellation argument

proof.text: Take $g\in B^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ with $ng\in B$. Write $g=a-b$ with $a,b\in B$. At every geometric point with lift to $U$, its image $g_{\bar x}=a_{\bar x}-b_{\bar x}$ in $M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ has $ng_{\bar x}\in M_{\bar x}$, so Step 2 gives $d_{\bar x}\in M_{\bar x}$ representing $g_{\bar x}$. Integrality gives $d_{\bar x}+b_{\bar x}=a_{\bar x}$ in the stalk. Stalks are the neighbourhood colimits of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. By [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] and the representatives and eventual-equality clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], choose a pointed etale refinement $V\to U$ and $d_V\in M(V)$ with $d_V+b|_V=a|_V$. Work on small skeletons in the enlarged universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Choosing such a neighbourhood for a geometric point over each point of $U$ gives a jointly surjective etale covering; no finite subcover is needed.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks), local-neighbourhood construction; filtered stalk argument

proof.text: On $V\times_U W$, the two local representatives satisfy $d_V+b=a=d_W+b$. Cancellation for sections, proved in Step 3, gives $d_V=d_W$ on this overlap. The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] therefore glues them to $d\in M(U)$, and also gives $d+b=a$ globally. It follows that $g=a-b=d$ in $B^{\rm gp}$, proving saturation. For $U=\varnothing$, the empty-cover sheaf axiom makes $M(U)$ the one-element monoid, which is integral saturated. This argument neither asserts finite generation of sections nor imposes any Noetherian condition on $X$.

source.place: Definition Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf-sets), applied to the etale coverings of Tag 0215; agent gluing argument

lean.statement: theorem EtaleLogStructure.integral_saturated_of_isFineSaturated {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : EtaleLogStructure X) (hM : M.IsFineSaturated) : (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X), Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := M.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalk x)) ∧ ∀ (g : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (M.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalk x)) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (∃ m : M.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalk x, Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of m = g ^ n) → ∃ m : M.toEtalePrelogStructure.stalk x, Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of m = g) ∧ ∀ U : X.Etale, Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U))) ∧ ∀ (g : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U))) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (∃ m : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U), Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of m = g ^ n) → ∃ m : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U), Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of m = g
